name: Advanced Citation Management Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for citation management intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for citation management intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple citation management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen citation management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. Keep citation management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Check that citation management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
5. Measure before optimizing any citation management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to citation management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Prefer the simplest citation management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. Keep citation management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated citation management concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of citation management correctness.
- Avoid introducing new citation management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about citation management over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
